$ cloud --help
--- stdout
usage: cloud [-h] {deploys,status,wait,logs,doctor} ...

cloud — what is deployed on Laravel Cloud, read from its API (ROADMAP B88).

positional arguments:
  {deploys,status,wait,logs,doctor}
    deploys             the last deploys
    status              the live commit against origin/main
    wait                block until a commit's deploy finishes
    logs                the site's logs, or one deploy's steps
    doctor              check the key, the token and what it resolves to

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

cloud — what is deployed on Laravel Cloud, read from its API (ROADMAP B88).

patchlamp.com runs on Laravel Cloud and a push to `main` deploys it. Until
this tool a session proved a deploy by probing the live site, and nobody could
read the site's logs from here. This reads both back.

  cloud deploys [-n 5]        # the last deploys: status, commit, branch, message, started, finished
  cloud status                # the commit that is live against origin/main, and any deploy in flight
  cloud wait [SHA]            # block until that commit's deploy succeeds or fails (default: origin/main)
  cloud logs [--since 1h]     # the site's application/access logs (--type, --query, --errors, -n)
  cloud logs --deploy [SHA]   # one deploy's build and deploy steps (default: the newest)
  cloud doctor                # the key, the token, the app and environment it resolves to

Options on every command: --app NAME|ID, --env NAME|ID (default: the app's
default environment; CLOUD_APP / CLOUD_ENV in the environment or the key file
do the same). --json on deploys/status/wait prints the same named fields as
JSON, never the API's own response.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 an error (bad token, unreachable, nothing to resolve);
`status` exits 3 when the live commit is not origin/main or a deploy is in
flight; `wait` exits 1 when the deploy failed and 2 when it timed out.

Read-only by construction. Every request goes through `_get()`, which builds
a GET and nothing else, whatever the token would allow (a test greps this file
for any other verb). The environment object the API returns carries the
production app's environment variables, which are the site's real secrets,
so this tool reads fields by name, keeps nothing on disk, and on an error
prints the HTTP status and a short reason, never the response body.

Config, by name, never printed:
  LARAVEL_CLOUD_TOKEN   ~/.config/claude-tools/env (view-only token from the Cloud UI)
  PATCHLAMP_REPO        optional; the local clone whose `origin` is compared (default ~/projects/patchlamp)
The key file is parsed here, never sourced by a shell: the token holds a `|`.
--- stderr
--- exit 0
